fr.recommendations:
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from the road in both directions.
• Keep the driveway clear of parked vehicles to allow emergency vehicles to reach the front of the residence.
• Trim any vegetation along the driveway edges that narrows the travel path or blocks sightlines to the front entrance.
• Cut back plants and shrubs growing close to the detached structure to keep a clear path around it for responders on foot.
• Identify and mark a secondary access route to the rear of the property if one exists, even if informal.
• Keep any gate or barrier controlling the single driveway access unlocked or equipped with a lock box accessible to emergency responders.
• Mark the walkway path to the detached structure so responders can locate it quickly at night or in low visibility.
• Keep the area between the main residence and the detached structure clear of stored materials, equipment, or debris that would block responder movement.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Mow or cut the tall grass area down before it dries out and becomes easier to ignite.
• Keep grass around the house and any outbuildings cut short throughout the dry season.
• Thin scattered shrubs that sit close to any structure to increase the open space between plants and walls.
• Remove dead or dry grass buildup that has collected against fences, walls, or outbuildings.
• Trim lower branches on scattered trees near structures so flames from ground-level grass cannot climb directly into the tree canopy.
• Clear any grass or shrub growth that has crept into the limited rear access area to keep that route passable for vehicles.
• Keep the rear access route visible and free of overhanging branches or encroaching shrubs so responders can reach the back of the property.
• Separate any woodpiles, equipment, or stored materials from surrounding grass and shrubs by moving them to a cleared area.
• Mow or clear a wider strip of grass immediately around any outbuildings that sit in or near the tall grass area.
